text:
A: Hello! Tomasz, from Walsall. You're Abena, yeah?
B: Yes, hello. Herne Hill, in London.
A: London, okay. Listen, I saw your picture, I said, this lady is teacher, or boss somewhere. Am I right?
B: (laughs) Neither, I'm afraid. I'm an interior designer. Part-time, for a small studio in Dulwich.
A: Interior designer. So you tell rich people what colour sofa.
B: Well. Sort of. I listen to what they want, which isn't always what they say, and then I find the pieces. Fabrics, furniture, lighting.
A: That's sales, you know? Same like me. I sell business energy on the phone. Takeaways, garages, salons. You find what they want, you don't let them off the line.
B: Erm, I suppose there's some overlap. I'd like to think I'm a little gentler about it.
A: Gentle is fine, if it works. Does it work?
B: Usually, yes. People end up spending a bit more than they planned, and they're happy about it.
A: Ha! That's good sales, that's the best sales. Listen, your studio, who is your energy supplier? Business tariff, yeah? I can save them money, I promise you.
B: (laughs) I have no idea. I'll leave that to the owner.
A: Okay, okay, I don't push. Little bit, maybe. So where you find furniture? Shops, auctions?
B: Vintage and antique shops mostly. Some suppliers. There's a mid-century sideboard in Crystal Palace I keep going back to see. Teak. Nine hundred pounds.
A: Nine hundred! For cupboard? Listen, you go in, you don't look at it. You look at something else. Then you ask, what about that one, by the way, and you say six, cash. They say no, you walk to the door. They call you back. Every time. I do this at car boot every Sunday, I get drill set for a fiver last week.
B: Well, I do negotiate with suppliers for clients, so I know the walk to the door. But for myself, I'm sort of hopeless. If I love something, it shows on my face.
A: That's the problem. Never love it. Not in the shop. Love it at home, after.
B: (laughs) That's actually very good advice.
A: Free advice. Next time, ten per cent.
B: Of course. What do you do when you're not selling, then?
A: Five-a-side Thursday, football, cars. I have BMW, keep it very clean. Barbecue in summer. You?
B: Galleries, mostly. Dulwich Picture Gallery, the South London Gallery. I collect a few small pieces, contemporary African artists.
A: Galleries, no. Honestly, last time I was in museum, school trip, Poland. I don't see the point, looking at pictures on wall.
B: Well, let me think how to put it. It's a bit like your car. You notice things other people don't. The lines, how it's made, someone's care in it. A painting is the same, if you give it a minute.
A: Hm. Car, okay, I understand car. Maybe if the gallery had BMW.
B: There are design museums that would, you know.
A: Really? Okay, that I go. Holidays, you travel?
B: Ghana every year or two, I'm from Accra. And small city trips, Lisbon, Copenhagen. Little hotels, galleries, markets.
A: Me, all-inclusive. Turkey, two years ago. Pool, buffet, pool bar, I don't move one week. Perfect.
B: That sounds very restful. I don't think I could sit still that long.
A: You must try. Listen, the buffet in that hotel, every night different, Turkish, Italian, and the pool bar guy, he knows my drink by second day —
